en.html:
Was this what they called a possessing spirit leaving the body? My own body, my own mind, and both had become so light that I was finding them unfamiliar.

Alive. Bas, that was the feeling.

No additional importance was coming attached to it.

Small.
Not heavy.
Someone, and no one in particular.

Just living.

...So in the end, had I been arrogant? Had I only now agreed to recognise myself at my actual size?

It seemed that way.

The way of heaven.
That phrase from last night came back to me.

<ruby>憑物<rt>つきもの</rt></ruby>が落ちた心地、と云うのだろうか。
　心身の軽さは、我が事ながら戸惑う程だった。

　生きている。
　ただ、そう感じる。

　そこに付加価値は何も無い。

　小さく。
　重からず。
　何者でもあり、何者でもなく。

　ただ生きている。

　……とどのつまり。
　自分は傲慢だったのかと、思う。

　等身大の自分自身を、今ようやく認めているのか。
　そう思う。

　――天道。
　昨夜聞いた一語を思い出す。

en.html: If a person's sins were for heaven to judge—and for the collective judgment of the world below, which reflected heaven—then what was I doing, taking the whole judgment into my own personal hands? That itself was arrogance.◆ ...Was that the matter? Probably... yes. One day I would be judged. The day of reckoning would come; I believed that. With that belief— I would live.
en.text:
If a person's sins were for heaven to judge—and for the collective judgment of the world below, which reflected heaven—then what was I doing, taking the whole judgment into my own personal hands? That itself was arrogance.◆

...Was that the matter?

Probably... yes.

One day I would be judged. The day of reckoning would come; I believed that.

With that belief—

I would live.

en.text:
Probably that was how it was.

The kitchen's cheerful rhythm came to my ears, and something filled me. Happiness—◆no. That was not quite the thing. But peace was there. A quietness inside.

Like soaking in a lake in summer. Time could pass at its own speed; I was in no hurry to assist it...
